annotations.title: Base and Column Structure
annotations.overview: The base is the broad lower foundation, and the column is the upright structure that supports the milling head above it.
annotations.function: Together they provide stiffness, carry the machine’s weight, and keep the working members in a stable relationship during cutting.
annotations.relationships: The knee rises against the column, while the head projects from it over the table and workholding area.
annotations.inspection: Look for clean bearing surfaces around the knee path, secure covers, sound mounting points, and chips or fluid collecting at the base.
annotations.safety: Keep clear of moving members and do not climb on the machine. Report loose anchors, damaged covers, or unusual vibration before use.

annotations.title: Knee and Elevation System
annotations.overview: The knee is the large movable casting beneath the table assembly, positioned between the base and the work surface.
annotations.function: It raises or lowers the table system to establish the vertical distance between the workpiece and the cutting tool.
annotations.relationships: The saddle and worktable sit above the knee, and the elevating drive moves the knee along the column.
annotations.inspection: Check the visible slide area for chips, damaged edges, leaking lubricant, and clearance between the knee, column, table, and nearby controls.
annotations.safety: Treat knee travel as a crushing hazard. Keep hands away from gaps between moving castings and never reach beneath a raised table assembly.

annotations.title: Z-Axis Elevating Drive
annotations.overview: The elevating drive is the hand-operated mechanism beside and beneath the knee that controls the table assembly’s height.
annotations.function: It turns mechanical elements that lift or lower the knee in small, controlled increments for setting tool height.
annotations.relationships: Its output supports the knee’s vertical motion, while the saddle and worktable move with the knee above it.
annotations.inspection: Check the handwheel, crank, shafts, and nearby guards for secure attachment, bent parts, damaged handles, or chips that could obstruct movement.
annotations.safety: Use controls only from a balanced position with the work area clear. Keep fingers away from rotating cranks and knee pinch points.

annotations.title: Table and Feed System
annotations.overview: The table and feed system is the central work-supporting assembly, combining the worktable with the mechanisms that position it.
annotations.function: It presents a secured workpiece to the cutter through controlled longitudinal, crosswise, and vertical positioning.
annotations.relationships: The worktable rides on the saddle, the saddle rests on the knee, and the vise clamps work near the cutter.
annotations.inspection: Look across the table area for trapped chips, damaged slots, loose handles, interference with the vise, and clear travel under the head.
annotations.safety: Keep hands outside the travel path while adjusting the table. Stop the spindle before measuring, clearing chips, or changing the setup.

annotations.title: Saddle and Y-Axis Carriage
annotations.overview: The saddle is the intermediate slide beneath the worktable, carrying the table across the knee in the front-to-back direction.
annotations.function: It provides crosswise positioning so the work can move under the rotating cutter without disturbing its clamped orientation.
annotations.relationships: The saddle supports the worktable above, travels on the knee below, and works with the table’s feed screw and handwheels.
annotations.inspection: Observe the exposed slide surfaces, gib area, hand controls, and travel clearance for chips, scoring, loose hardware, or contact with the column.
annotations.safety: Keep fingers clear of saddle gaps and slideways. Do not reach across a moving table or toward a cutter to adjust this axis.

annotations.title: T-Slotted Worktable
annotations.overview: The worktable is the long slotted surface where a vise, fixture, or workpiece is secured for milling.
annotations.function: Its slots accept clamping hardware and allow the workholding arrangement to be placed where the cutter can reach the work.
annotations.relationships: The table rides on the saddle, carries the vise, and moves the clamped work beneath the spindle and cutter.
annotations.inspection: Inspect slot edges, the tabletop, clamps, and open areas around the vise for burrs, chips, damaged threads, or unsecured items.
annotations.safety: Secure work and clamps before rotation, and keep them below the tool path. Never brush chips away near a rotating cutter.

annotations.title: X-Axis Feed Screw and Handwheels
annotations.overview: The feed screw and handwheels are the manual controls at the table ends that move the worktable lengthwise.
annotations.function: Turning a handwheel advances or retracts the table, allowing the work to pass beneath the cutter at a chosen position.
annotations.relationships: They move the worktable over the saddle and coordinate with crosswise and vertical positioning to locate the work in three directions.
annotations.inspection: Check handwheels, handles, dials, screw supports, and table-end clearance for damage, looseness, sharp edges, or interference with nearby equipment.
annotations.safety: Avoid loose sleeves and jewelry around rotating handwheels. Keep hands clear when power feed or any table motion is active.

annotations.title: Milling Head and Drive
annotations.overview: The milling head is the upper assembly that houses the spindle drive and projects the rotating tool over the work area.
annotations.function: It supplies rotary power to a cutting tool while its housing establishes the tool’s position above the table.
annotations.relationships: The head mounts to the column, drives the spindle below it, and works over the table, vise, and moving workpiece.
annotations.inspection: Check head covers, mounting joints, control locations, tool clearance, and signs of oil leakage or vibration around the drive housing.
annotations.safety: Do not open covers or reach near the spindle while it can move. Stop the machine before investigating noise, vibration, or a loose cover.

annotations.title: Drive Motor and Selector Controls
annotations.overview: The drive motor and selector controls are the power source and switches associated with choosing the mill’s operating condition.
annotations.function: They provide and direct power for spindle rotation, allowing an appropriate speed or direction to be selected for the task.
annotations.relationships: The motor drives the head mechanism, while the controls are used before the spindle turns above the table and workholding.
annotations.inspection: Read visible markings and inspect buttons, levers, motor housing, wiring covers, and selector positions for damage, missing parts, or unclear labels.
annotations.safety: Make setting changes only when motion is stopped unless machine instructions state otherwise. Keep hands away from rotating tools while using controls.

annotations.title: Spindle, Arbor, and Cutter
annotations.overview: The spindle, arbor, and cutter form the rotating cutting end of the mill directly above the workholding area.
annotations.function: The spindle turns the arbor and cutter so the tool’s edges can remove material from a securely held workpiece.
annotations.relationships: This assembly hangs below the milling head and approaches the work as the table and knee position the vise beneath it.
annotations.inspection: Look for a properly seated tool assembly, secure retention, adequate clearance to clamps, and any damage or chips near the cutting edges.
annotations.safety: Treat the cutter as sharp even when stopped and as an entanglement hazard when rotating. Keep hands, tools, and clothing outside its path.

annotations.title: Head Positioning Hardware
annotations.overview: The head positioning hardware includes the joints, locks, and adjustment parts that support the milling head on the column.
annotations.function: It allows the head to be located and secured so the spindle and cutter remain in the intended position above the work.
annotations.relationships: It connects the head and drive to the column, setting the cutter’s relationship to the worktable, vise, and workpiece.
annotations.inspection: Check visible locks, adjustment screws, handles, and mounting faces for secure seating, missing hardware, damage, or clearance problems around the head.
annotations.safety: Support and secure the head before releasing any lock. Keep clear of suspended or shifting parts and follow approved service instructions for adjustments.

annotations.title: Workholding Vise
annotations.overview: The workholding vise is the clamping device on the worktable that holds a workpiece steady during milling.
annotations.function: Its fixed and moving jaws grip suitable work so cutting forces do not shift the part while the table positions it.
annotations.relationships: The vise bolts to the slotted worktable and presents the workpiece beneath the spindle, arbor, and cutter.
annotations.inspection: Check jaw faces, clamping screw, mounting hardware, chip buildup, and tool clearance to confirm the work and vise can remain secure.
annotations.safety: Clamp the work securely and keep hands clear before spindle rotation. Never hold a workpiece by hand against a milling cutter.
